articles.title: Rochdale Council Faces £15 Million Budget Deficit by 2029
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Council is projected to face a £15 million budget deficit by 2029 if no action is taken, according to the latest financial forecast presented to town hall officials.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Council is facing a projected budget deficit of £15.227 million by the financial year 2029/30 if no measures are implemented. The latest budget forecast, presented to town hall officials, highlights that this shortfall is anticipated due to rising wage costs, inflation, and increased pressures in adult social care and children’s services.

The finance team has expressed uncertainty regarding the annual government funding settlement, which complicates future budget planning. Budget documents indicate a risk that the finance settlement for 2029/30 may not include a continuation of the Recovery Grant, which is currently confirmed only until 2028/29 and amounts to approximately £15 million.

In adult social care, the 'real living wage' is increasing at a rate higher than anticipated, further straining financial resources. An additional allocation of £1.5 million per year has been incorporated into future cost estimates. Overspending in children’s services has also exceeded initial forecasts, a trend that has been noted in recent years, according to the meeting held on July 28.

Councillor Daniel Meredith remarked on the ongoing efforts to establish new care homes and children’s homes, stating that significant work is being done to address the challenges in these services. The council has made savings of £204.5 million from its revenue budget since 2010/11, but the projected gaps indicate that savings of £6 million will be necessary by 2028/29, escalating to £15 million by 2029/30.

articles.title: Neglected toddler admitted to hospital 19 days after social services closed case
articles.excerpt: A 19-month-old girl, referred to as Child K1, was admitted to hospital in critical condition after social services closed her case, revealing severe neglect and malnutrition.
articles.content_html:
ONGOING STORY — Updated 29 July 2026 at 10:49. 9 source updates have been combined into this article.

A 19-month-old girl, referred to as Child K1, was admitted to hospital in critical condition after social services closed her case, revealing severe neglect and malnutrition.

Latest update

A woman died at Lakeside Residential Home on 25 July 2026. Lynn Horrocks, 77, was pronounced dead at the scene. Police confirmed there are no suspicious circumstances surrounding her death.

Authorities are seeking information regarding her next of kin. Anyone who may have information is encouraged to come forward.

The death has been reported to the coroner, and a post-mortem examination will take place to determine the cause of death.

Our thoughts are with the family and all those affected.

Earlier developments

A 19-month-old girl, referred to as Child K1, was admitted to hospital in critical condition after social services closed her case, revealing severe neglect and malnutrition.

A 19-month-old girl, referred to as Child K1, was admitted to hospital in critical condition 19 days after social services closed her case, according to a Child Safeguarding Practice Review (CSPR) in Rochdale. The review found that the toddler was severely neglected, weighing just 9.7lb (4.4kg) at the time of her admission, which is less than half the expected weight for her age.

The report described the child as "incredibly emaciated" and noted she had no fatty tissue on her body, with "paper-thin skin" and open pressure sores extending along her back, hips and bottom. The review indicated that the child was suffering from severe dehydration and malnutrition, which could have led to death if emergency treatment had not been administered in time.

Concerns about the child's welfare had been raised multiple times prior to her hospital admission. A family member initially alerted hospital staff in April 2024, stating that a mother, who was 17 when the child was born, was neglecting her. Despite these warnings, social services concluded that the mother was "willing to accept support" and closed the case after a multi-agency strategy meeting in February 2025, stating that the threshold for further action had not been met.

Following an anonymous tip in December 2024, social workers visited the home and confirmed the child's poor condition. However, they were unable to secure the mother's consent for social care involvement. The review highlighted a series of missed appointments and a lack of engagement from the mother, which ultimately led to the child's critical condition upon hospital admission.

The review revealed that the child was covered in sores and had no fatty tissue on her body. Medical staff noted her skin was "paper-thin" and that she displayed signs of severe dehydration. The case was closed despite concerns raised about a mother’s ability to care for her, as she had reportedly avoided contact with social workers and health visitors for weeks.

The review, conducted by expert reviewer Nicki Walker-Hall, highlighted that the child's grandmother had taken her to the hospital after she refused to eat. During this visit, family members informed hospital staff that the child was being neglected. Following this, the case was referred to Rochdale's Children's Social Care team, which initially assessed the mother as willing to accept support.

However, after an anonymous tip-off in December 2024 alleging severe neglect, social workers visited the home but were unable to secure the mother's consent for further intervention. A multi-agency strategy meeting concluded that the threshold for further action had not been met, leading to the case being closed. Nineteen days later, the child was admitted to critical care, suffering from multiple complications that could have been life-threatening without timely medical intervention.

  • 29 July 2026, 06:09: Neglected toddler admitted to hospital 19 days after social services closed case

articles.title: Rochdale Veteran Seeks Justice Following Nuclear Tests
articles.excerpt: John Morris, a Rochdale veteran exposed to nuclear tests in the 1950s, expresses renewed hope for justice following the appointment of Prime Minister Andy Burnham, who supports an independent inquiry.
articles.content_html:
A man from Rochdale who was exposed to nuclear tests in the 1950s has expressed renewed hope for justice following the appointment of Prime Minister Andy Burnham. John Morris, now 88, was sent to Christmas Island in the Pacific Ocean at the age of 18, where he witnessed a series of nuclear detonations conducted by the Ministry of Defence (MoD).

Morris is part of a group of veterans who have lodged a criminal complaint against the MoD, claiming they have been denied justice regarding the health issues they suffered as a result of the tests. Many veterans have reported serious medical problems and are calling for an independent inquiry into their treatment. Burnham has previously supported the veterans' cause, stating that there is clear evidence of misconduct in public office. He has indicated that he backs a judicial review into the matter, which has given Morris and others hope for a resolution after years of campaigning.

The MoD has stated that compensation is available through the War Pensions Scheme, but many veterans feel this is insufficient. Morris believes that with Burnham's support, there is a chance for a thorough investigation into their claims. He has said that the new Prime Minister has finally given him hope of getting justice, as he continues to advocate for the rights of veterans affected by the nuclear tests.

In 2025, when Burnham was mayor of Greater Manchester, he expressed his view that the investigation into the treatment of veterans could not wait any longer, especially following the 80th anniversary of VE Day. Morris and his fellow veterans are now looking to the new Prime Minister to take decisive action on their behalf.

articles.title: Firefighters Tackle Waste Fire in Rochdale Overnight
articles.excerpt: A fire broke out in Smallbridge, Rochdale, on Friday evening, prompting a response from firefighters who worked through the night to extinguish the flames and monitor the aftermath.
articles.content_html:
A fire broke out in an open area on Spring Mill Walk in Smallbridge at around 8:15pm on Friday, July 24. Aerial images captured the impact of the fire, which burned overnight and produced large plumes of black smoke visible across Rochdale.

Firefighters worked throughout the night to extinguish the flames and remained on the scene until around 1pm on Saturday, damping down hotspots and monitoring the aftermath. Dramatic photos on social media showed the extent of the fire, which involved a large quantity of waste at the site.

Officials from the Environment Agency were called in, and the local council was alerted due to the nature of the incident. Pictures taken by a drone camera later revealed a significant area of scorched earth and debris left behind by the fire.

No injuries have been reported as a result of the fire. Fire crews are expected to continue monitoring the site in the coming days.
